The awk condition didn't match (probably because the leading whitespace is different — the actual line is "      - ./nginx/nginx.conf:..." with 6 spaces). I'll fix awk to match on `.*\./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/conf\.d/default\.conf:ro$`.

Given the complexity of editing three places, I'll write out the entire corrected docker-compose.dev.yml. It's safer to reconstruct it from the backup using targeted awk substitutions:

1. Line 214: replace `- ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro` → `- ./nginx/default.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro` (exact string replacement).
2. QGIS command block: replace the block starting from `  qgis-server:` with the `command:` line, up through the terminating `"` of the folded scalar. This is complex. Alternative: replace the qgis-server command with a simpler, more robust approach — a script file? The dev compose's command is inline.

An even cleaner approach for qgis-server: keep the same structure while fixing the heredoc into a properly working form:

```yaml
  qgis-server:
    ...
    command: >
      sh -c "
        mkdir -p /etc/postgresql-common &&
        {
          echo \"[${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}]\";
          echo \"host=db\";
          echo \"port=5432\";
          echo \"dbname=${DB_NAME}\";
          echo \"user=${QGIS_DB_USER}\";
          echo \"password=${QGIS_DB_PASSWORD}\";
          echo \"sslmode=disable\";
        } > /etc/postgresql-common/pg_service.conf &&
        mkdir -p /var/www/data/qgis &&
        ln -sf /usr/lib/cgi-bin/qgis_mapserv.fcgi /var/www/data/qgis/qgis_mapserv.fcgi &&
        rm -f /tmp/.X99-lock &&
        fc-cache &&
        /usr/bin/Xvfb :99 -ac -screen 0 1280x1024x16 +extension GLX +render -noreset >/dev/null &
        sleep 2 &&
        grep -q 'client_max_body_size' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf || sed -i '/http {/a \    client_max_body_size 500M;' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf &&
        nginx &&
        spawn-fcgi -F 2 -u www-data -g www-data -d /var/lib/qgis -P /run/qgis.pid -p 9993 -- /usr/lib/cgi-bin/qgis_mapserv.fcgi &&
        tail -f /dev/null
      "
```

The folded scalar (>) folds newlines into spaces. A quoted `\"` remains as `\"` inside the double-quoted YAML scalar → when the YAML value (a string) is passed to sh, `\"` becomes a literal `"`. Wait, in a YAML double-quoted scalar, `\"` is an escape that produces a literal `"` character. So the string that sh -c receives contains `echo "[qonnectra]"`. Good.

Watch out for `\` inside the YAML double-quoted scalar: `\\` is required to produce a literal backslash. Inside the echo line: `echo \"[${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}]\"` — `[` `]` are fine. Inside the sed: `sed -i '/http {/a \    client_max_body_size 500M;'` — the `\` before the spaces: in a YAML double-quoted scalar, a single `\` followed by a space is an invalid escape! YAML double-quoted strings only allow specific escapes: \", \\, \/, \n, \t, etc. `\ ` is invalid YAML. The original file uses a block scalar (`>`) for the qgis command — that's why the backslashes were safe. So my replacement must also use the block scalar style (`>`), not double quotes.

Wait — the original file is:
```yaml
    command: >
      sh -c "
        mkdir -p ...
        ...
      "
```
It's a block scalar with embedded double quotes. In a block scalar, quotes have no special meaning; they're just part of the string. So the value is:
`sh -c "\n  mkdir ...\n  cat > ... <<EOF\n...EOF\n  mkdir -p...\n...tail -f /dev/null\n  "`
And sh -c executes that.

So the fix in block-scalar form is:

```
    command: >
      sh -c "
        mkdir -p /etc/postgresql-common &&
        {
          echo '[${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}]';
          echo 'host=db';
          echo 'port=5432';
          echo 'dbname=${DB_NAME}';
          echo 'user=${QGIS_DB_USER}';
          echo 'password=${QGIS_DB_PASSWORD}';
          echo 'sslmode=disable';
        } > /etc/postgresql-common/pg_service.conf &&
        mkdir -p /var/www/data/qgis &&
        ln -sf /usr/lib/cgi-bin/qgis_mapserv.fcgi /var/www/data/qgis/qgis_mapserv.fcgi &&
        rm -f /tmp/.X99-lock &&
        fc-cache &&
        /usr/bin/Xvfb :99 -ac -screen 0 1280x1024x16 +extension GLX +render -noreset >/dev/null &
        sleep 2 &&
        grep -q 'client_max_body_size' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf || sed -i '/http {/a \    client_max_body_size 500M;' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf &&
        nginx &&
        spawn-fcgi -F 2 -u www-data -g www-data -d /var/lib/qgis -P /run/qgis.pid -p 9993 -- /usr/lib/cgi-bin/qgis_mapserv.fcgi &&
        tail -f /dev/null
      "
```

In the block scalar, all lines are joined with spaces. `sed -i '/http {/a \    client_max_body_size 500M;'` is inside double quotes in the sh string — the `\` before the spaces is fine in a block scalar.

Single quotes inside the sh -c double-quoted string: fine.
